blockland.settings.perf.benchmark.note: Turns the camera on the spot for about two minutes: frame times with every optimization off and on in turn, two full section rebuilds each, timed, and finally a held frame compared pixel by pixel between off and on. Runs in a world only; do not touch mouse or keyboard meanwhile, Esc or any screen stops it. With OP rights the world is frozen with /tick freeze while it runs.
blockland.settings.perf.show_timings.not: Measures every stage of each frame on the CPU and the GPU (timestamp queries read back 4 frames later, never waiting for the GPU); the F3 screen's right side lists the most expensive ones (ms, CPU / GPU). Measuring costs a little itself.
blockland.settings.perf.background_fps.n: While the game window is not in front (you switched to another window) it draws at most this many frames, leaving the GPU to the program in front. Without a cap a covered game window keeps rendering flat out: with two clients on one computer, the one behind takes the whole GPU and the one in front freezes now and then. All the way right means no cap (vanilla's Max Framerate still applies); never applies during a benchmark.
blockland.settings.perf.opt.gl_state.not: Vanilla sets texture levels and filtering, samplers, buffer and framebuffer bindings, polygon mode, viewport and scissor box again on every draw even when they already hold that value. Only calls that change nothing for any draw are skipped; the GPU sees exactly the same state.
blockland.settings.perf.opt.immediate_up: Entity, particle and block entity vertices and indices used to be written over one buffer again and again, so the driver had to wait or copy while the GPU still read it. They now go one after another into a ring buffer; the data and the draw order are unchanged.
blockland.settings.perf.opt.terrain_draw: Each section's terrain draw no longer allocates temporary objects or binds the same vertex array and index buffer again; the data sent to the GPU is byte for byte the same.
blockland.settings.perf.opt.section_mesh: Rebuilding section meshes when blocks change or a map loads: vertices read straight from the model's arrays, light and occlusion cached for the whole section; the vertices are byte for byte the same. Switching rebuilds every section once.
blockland.settings.perf.opt.enclosed_blo: When chunk meshes are rebuilt, blocks whose six faces are all hidden by full neighbours are no longer checked face by face (they would draw nothing anyway); the meshes are byte for byte the same. Switching rebuilds every section once.
Solid and cutout faces are grouped by the way they face; groups facing away from the camera are not sent to the GPU (its back-face culling would discard them anyway) and the rest are drawn in their original order; the picture is pixel for pixel the same. Also used for the real far chunks. Switching rebuilds every section once.
blockland.settings.perf.opt.far_hidden_g: Parts of the real far chunks no line of sight from outside can reach (sealed caves, blocks buried on all sides) are not meshed; the camera is never inside those chunks, so the picture is exactly the same, with less video memory and meshing time.
blockland.settings.perf.opt.section_copi: A section rebuild used to copy every block entity of the whole chunk column; now only the ones inside the section, which are all it reads.
Grass, leaf and water colours blend the biomes around; each sampled biome's colour is worked out once and the blend is the same integer sum. Mostly speeds up map loading.
blockland.settings.perf.opt.compile_queu: On a map switch the compile queue removed its many cancelled tasks one by one (slower the more there are); now they go in one sweep and the next task chosen is the same.
blockland.settings.perf.opt.particles.no: Dead particles are removed in one sweep instead of one by one from the middle of the queue, no temporary objects per particle and frame, and each block's brightness is looked up once per particle pass; order, positions and brightness are unchanged.
blockland.settings.perf.opt.shadow_batch: Every shadow cascade draws the sections around again; each used to be submitted on its own with all state set again, now each cascade submits them in one batch in the same order, and gathering them makes almost no garbage.
blockland.settings.perf.opt.shadow_tile_: A cascade's tile used to be emptied by drawing a full-tile quad that writes depth; the GPU's own clear does it now, with the same depth of 1 everywhere.
blockland.settings.perf.opt.shadow_entit: Entity shadows: only what is read

Geometry the shadow map throws away (emissive, additive layers) is no longer transformed first, and the normals and colours its shader never reads are not worked out per vertex; uploads rotate through buffers instead of waiting for the last frame.
blockland.settings.perf.opt.shadow_culli: Besides its bounding sphere, a section must also reach a cascade with its box in the sun's view (padded by how far the loaded block models stick out of their blocks, measured when they load); the sections it drops could not draw into that cascade anyway. Off while resources reload.
blockland.settings.perf.opt.motion_blur_: Motion blur finds the largest motion in each tile; one pixel used to read the whole tile serially, now the maximum is taken along rows and then columns, picking exactly the same motion.
blockland.settings.perf.opt.post_uniform: The post passes' constants are written only when they change, each pass with its own block, never overwritten while the GPU still reads it; the GPU reads the same values.
blockland.settings.perf.opt.post_dead_wo: Temporal anti-aliasing reads the hand's motion only on hand and weapon pixels, and frame generation no longer runs an extra pass to clear alpha for the HUD; the results are the same.
blockland.settings.perf.opt.viewmodel_ba: Consecutive hand and weapon draws that share their state are submitted as one, in the same order; motion vectors no longer make a new matrix per draw.
blockland.settings.perf.opt.impact_pools: Debris, sparks and stains used to scan their whole pool several times per frame, even for one stain left; now only live entries are visited and a stain's clipping is kept while nothing about it changes.
blockland.settings.perf.opt.frame_garbag: Motion blur, dynamic lights and poses no longer make objects or build strings per entity when they visit the entities around each frame, so there is less garbage to collect.

blockland.settings.language_note: Switching reloads the resources; after a moment the whole interface, lobby included, uses the new language.
blockland.settings.scope_sensitivity.not: Each magnification has its own aim sensitivity: the 1× class covers iron sights, red dots and holographic sights, the 2× to 10×+ classes cover scopes (everything above 10× uses 10×+). A scope already turns slower by its current power (the picture moves as fast as the bare view); these multipliers apply on top, 1.00 keeps that. Powers between two classes (a variable scope's 9×, or the picture easing to a new power) interpolate between the neighbouring classes in log space, so sensitivity changes smoothly with the power.
blockland.settings.scope.dim_outside: Darken the view around a raised scope
blockland.settings.scope.note: Magnified scopes render their own magnified picture in the eyepiece (picture in picture) while the view around them stays normal; aiming focuses on the sight (a scope's eyepiece) and the surroundings blur more towards the screen edges; higher quality is sharper and costs more. With a shader pack, or with this set to Off, the whole view zooms behind a scope mask instead. Scope sensitivity is set per magnification in the Sensitivity section above.
blockland.settings.camera.note: Camera impact: how hard shots, reload slams, landings and melee hits jolt and shake the view. Movement sway: the rise and fall of footsteps and the body's lean while walking and running. Impacts calm down by themselves while aiming so the sights stay true; lower them if the motion feels uncomfortable.
blockland.settings.impacts.fluid_physics: Fluid physics (debris in water, bubbles, bullet trails)
blockland.settings.graphics.soaking.note: Creatures out of the water drip and dry in about 45 seconds (slower in the rain); the weapon in your hands stays wet and beaded with water too.
blockland.settings.graphics.lens_water.n: Right after leaving the water, drops cling to the lens: they refract the picture, slide down leaving trails and dry within a few seconds; under water the picture wavers gently.
blockland.settings.impacts.note: Rounds and blades striking blocks, creatures and water throw debris, dust, sparks, blood drops or splashes by material; the hit angle and body part, the round and the energy it has left, the target's motion, rain, snow and water all change the effect. Blood drops stick to floors, walls and ceilings, run down walls, dry, and wash out in the rain. Fluid physics makes debris sink or float and drift with the current, rounds leave a trail of bubbles under water, and sparks die in water. Higher quality throws more pieces and shows them farther away; dust is the most expensive part, turn it off first when the frame rate drops.
blockland.settings.section.rgb: Custom colour (edits the colour picked above)
blockland.settings.allow_invites_note: When off, nobody can send you a party invite. Stored on the server, so it follows you to any computer.
blockland.settings.graphics.enabled_note: Master switch for upscaling, anti-aliasing, lighting and post-processing; off = vanilla rendering (weapons keep their studio lighting). A preset sets everything below at once; changing any value afterwards makes it Custom.
blockland.settings.graphics.display.note: Applies to the whole picture, menus included. Stretch fills the window (4:3 stretched makes everything look wider); black bars keep the picture's shape. A resolution above the window's supersamples (sharper, slower); below it runs faster but looks softer.
Default: NVIDIA picks the model per mode (K for DLAA / Quality / Balanced, M for Performance, L for Ultra Performance) and follows the NVIDIA App's DLSS override. J, K, L, M force one model for every mode: K is the steadiest, J ghosts a little less but may flicker, M is sharper, L suits very low render resolutions.
blockland.settings.graphics.dlss_frame_g: 2× is Frame Generation, 3× and up Multi Frame Generation (RTX 50 series)
Up to %s× on this GPU: 2× is Frame Generation, 3× and up Multi Frame Generation

Frames are then presented through DLSS's Vulkan swapchain, with Reflex required; nothing is generated in pause menus, loading screens or while the game window is not in front. V-sync has no effect with frame generation (DLSS does not support it on Vulkan), the frame rate limit applies to rendered frames, and motion blur is halved.

The blocks around you are kept as voxels and every pixel traces rays into them: light bounces between blocks (coloured indirect light, glowing blocks lighting their surroundings, sunlit faces bouncing sunlight) and ray traced ambient occlusion replaces the screen-space one. Demanding on the GPU.
Low: half resolution, 1 ray per pixel; Medium: half, 2 rays; High: full resolution, 2 rays; Ultra: full, 4 rays that go further.

blockland.settings.graphics.world_lighti: World lighting (sun shadows, dynamic lights, emissive)
Switching world lighting reloads resources; it applies when the settings close.
blockland.settings.graphics.shadow_penum: Shadows stay sharp where an object touches the ground and soften with distance, like real sunlight. Off: only the softness above (a fixed-width edge).
blockland.settings.graphics.light_colors: Light colours apply with world lighting, block light (torches, lava …) included; ray tracing and the volumetric clouds use the same colours.
blockland.settings.graphics.fog.note: Volumetric fog: haze thinning with height, ground mist in the low land at dawn, at dusk and in rain; sunlight through trees, windows and gaps in the clouds makes shafts, and torches and muzzle flashes glow in it.
blockland.settings.graphics.fog.off_note: Off leaves only a thin fade where the render distance ends; fog under water, in lava and powder snow, and from blindness or darkness stays.
blockland.settings.graphics.shader_sun_m: The sun and the moon are drawn by a shader instead of vanilla's textures: where the shadows come from; the sun with limb darkening and a corona, redder towards the horizon; the moon a sphere lit in vanilla's phase, with maria, craters and earthshine on its dark side, covering the stars behind it.
blockland.settings.graphics.physical_sky: Re-shades the sky by atmospheric scattering (Rayleigh + Mie): the zenith keeps vanilla's colour, the horizon pales, a glow surrounds the sun, sunsets redden and moonlit nights turn deep blue; greyer in rain. Stars, sun, moon and rain are kept and the horizon still meets the fog seamlessly.
blockland.settings.graphics.volumetric_c: Three layers of clouds with real depth in place of vanilla's: small cumulus low, large cumulus higher up and a high altostratus sheet, casting drifting shadows; rain closes the low clouds into an overcast, clears the high cumulus and thickens the altostratus; they follow the time of day, the weather and the light colours. Needs world lighting.
Volumetric clouds running, vanilla's clouds hidden
Starts once you are in a world
Shows the real terrain beyond the loaded chunks (sent by the server, up to 32768 blocks): the farther away, the coarser its cells — detailed near, only the shape far off — so memory and frame time hardly grow with the distance. Seen areas are cached on this computer and appear at once next time. Needs the render pipeline.
blockland.settings.graphics.far_terrain_: Higher detail means finer cells at the same distance (about 7 / 5 / 3.5 / 2.6 pixels per cell) and more data and vertices.

Out to this many chunks the far terrain keeps every block (the same blocks and textures as the game); only beyond it do its cells grow. Below the render distance it counts as the render distance. Larger is sharper, and takes more video memory and loading.
blockland.settings.graphics.far_chunks.n: Beyond the render distance, the server's real chunks are drawn with vanilla's own block renderer (blocks, textures, water, plants and light all from the real chunks) out to the real chunk distance. Within the full-detail distance it is block for block, exactly like vanilla; farther out each cell becomes a cube of 2, 4, 8 … blocks (still the real block there), the cube doubling as the distance doubles — that far a block is smaller than a pixel anyway, so it looks the same as drawing every block, while memory and video memory do not multiply with the distance. Only where the server has not generated the chunks yet does the far terrain fill in. The first time you look that far, the server has to generate the real chunks in the background (thousands of chunks take hours); generated areas appear at once from then on.
blockland.settings.graphics.far_chunk_fu: Within this many chunks the real chunks are drawn block by block; only beyond it do blocks merge into larger cubes. Larger looks sharper and needs more memory and video memory (at least 4 chunks beyond the render distance).
blockland.settings.graphics.far_chunks.s: Real chunks: %s drawn / %s placed, %s in memory, %s pending, %s MB video memory
blockland.settings.graphics.vanilla.dist: Within the render distance the game draws its full chunks, beyond it the far terrain carries on; the server's view distance caps it.
blockland.settings.graphics.vanilla.chun: Threaded: sections are built in the background, the steadiest frame rate; semi-blocking: blocks you place or break update at once; fully blocking: every nearby section updates at once, the most frame time.
blockland.settings.graphics.far_terrain_: How hazy the distant air is: at 100% the far end is about 70% haze and the land stays clear to half way; 0 is perfectly clear.
blockland.settings.graphics.far_atmosphe: Far land looks as the eye sees it: bluer and lower in contrast the farther it is (aerial perspective); from about a kilometre on, detail softens and outlines merge; on clear hot days far ground near the horizon wobbles in the heated air. Near things are untouched.
%s blocks: %s / %s tiles drawn, %s cells, %s MB GPU
blockland.graphics.status.far.server: The server offers no far terrain in this world
blockland.settings.graphics.rain_wetness: In rainy biomes, blocks out in the rain darken and gleam, puddles gather in low spots of flat ground with rain rings on them, and creatures and the weapons in their hands get wet and beaded with drops. It all dries slowly after the rain. Needs world lighting.
Water and puddles mirror what really stands around them (what is on screen); beyond the picture they still reflect the sky. Needs world lighting.
blockland.settings.graphics.water_ripple: Creatures wading, swimming and falling into water, swings aimed at it, blocks placed in it and rounds entering it raise ripples and splashes along their motion; running in the rain kicks up the water standing on the ground.
blockland.settings.graphics.wind.note: Gusts sweep across the ground, bending and shaking grass, flowers, crops, vines and leaves, harder in rain and thunderstorms; creatures walking through plants push them aside, and they swing back a while after. Water plants sway slowly with the current. Needs world lighting.

blockland.settings.graphics.weapon_light: Weapons lit by the world (sun, shadows, lights)
The value is a shutter angle: everything that moves on screen while the shutter is open leaves a smear, at any frame rate (360° = 1/30 s exposure, 180° = 1/60 s, the film standard). Motion blur covers the view turning and moving and other players, mobs, items and the like moving themselves; arm and weapon motion blur smears the first-person arms and weapon by their own movement (sway, recoil, reloads, inspects). Moving things smear over what is behind them, and the background never smears into the weapon. Higher quality takes more samples for smoother smears. Drag to the left to switch one off.

blockland.monster.creeper_zombie.skill.d: Lights its fuse and blows up 1.3 s later (slowed while it burns), hurting the humans around it and dying with them. Passive "Sympathetic Blast": goes off 0.5 s after it dies.
blockland.monster.ghast_lord.desc: The king of the Nether's ghasts: it hangs back and rains fireballs on the survivors.
blockland.monster.ghast_lord.skill.desc: Shoots a ghast fireball where you aim. It speeds up as it flies and explodes on the first survivor or block it hits, hurting the survivors around it (breaks no blocks, flies through allies). A punch can knock it back.
blockland.monster.blind.desc: A blindfolded infected that feels its way by sound: it mends the infected around it, and humans who come close are plunged into darkness.
blockland.monster.blind.skill.desc: Whispers to heal every infected ally within 3 blocks for 20 health (not itself). Passive "Shroud of Darkness": humans within 1 block go blind.
blockland.magazine.tommy_drum.desc: The classic 50-round drum: keeps firing far longer, but reloads and aims noticeably slower.
blockland.magazine.ks3_tube.desc: Standard-length tube magazine, loaded one shell at a time.
blockland.magazine.ks3_tube_ext.desc: A tube running out to the muzzle: two more shells, a heavier front end and slightly slower aiming.
blockland.magazine.usp_extended.desc: 18-round extended magazine; slightly slower to reload and aim.
blockland.magazine.usp_dual_standard.des: A 12-round magazine in each gun, 24 rounds in all.
blockland.magazine.usp_dual_extended.des: An 18-round extended magazine in each gun, 36 rounds in all; slightly slower to reload.
blockland.attachment.heavy_stock.desc: Solid adjustable stock with a cheek riser and a thick recoil pad: recoil -25%, noticeably slower aiming, slightly wider hip-fire spread.
blockland.attachment.wire_stock.desc: Minimal folding wire stock: recoil -8% at almost no cost to aiming speed.
blockland.attachment.vertical_grip.desc: Vertical foregrip under the handguard: recoil -12%, slightly slower to aim (+5%).
blockland.attachment.angled_grip.desc: Low angled foregrip: faster to aim (-7%), recoil -5%.
blockland.attachment.bipod.desc: Folding bipod (machine guns and sniper rifles only): recoil -18%, but heavier: slower to aim (+12%), hip-fire spread +10%.
blockland.attachment.tommy_grip.desc: The Thompson's own finger-grooved walnut foregrip: handles exactly like the gun as issued.

blockland.settings.perf.opt.shadow_sorti: Shadow casters sorted towards the sun

The sections nearest the sun are drawn first, so the ground under the trees and the caves under the ground fail the GPU's early depth test instead of being rasterised and written. Each shadow texel ends at the least depth covering it whatever the order, so the shadow map is byte for byte the same.
blockland.perf.report.only: Only this optimization compared (all others on): %s
blockland.settings.perf.opt.shadow_reuse: Each cascade's terrain depth is kept on the side; while the cascade's place, the sun, the camera position, the section meshes in it and the block textures (each game tick) stay the same, the terrain is not drawn again but copied back and the entities drawn over it — byte for byte what drawing it again gives. Saves most while standing still (the sun stands still in matches); takes video memory the size of the shadow map (about 256 MB on ultra).
